messages:
anika-support: Urgent — AcmeCorp reporting sudden burst of 429s since 09:12 UTC. They have a Dedicated pool 'acme-prod-gold' but traces show traffic landing on coldpool and getting throttled. Can we triage?

jordan-eng-sre: Looking at control-plane traces now. Early sign: header parsing oddity. Tenant sent 'X-Redwood-Tier: Gold' (capital G). Our tier lookup seems case-sensitive so it fell back to default policy that picked coldpool.

lee-runtime: That would explain autoscale not firing — requests hit shared cold pool where tenant-scale is disabled, so throttles appear even though they have dedicated capacity. Can you paste the exact request headers?

anika-support: Here are the raw headers customer captured:
```
X-Api-Key: sk_live_xxx
X-Redwood-Tier: Gold
X-Tenant-ID: acme-123
User-Agent: AcmeSDK/1.4.2
```

jordan-eng-sre: Confirmed on my local repro. controlplane change in 2026.02.3 lower-cased header names but did NOT normalize tier *values*. Tier mapping is an exact match, so 'Gold' != 'gold'. Repro: send 'Gold' -> routed to coldpool; send 'gold' -> correct dedicated pool.

maria-plat-eng: Short-term mitigation: add normalization in controlplane to lowercase tier values before lookup, and add a canary. Workaround for customer: they can set explicit pool header `X-Redwood-Pool: acme-prod-gold` or update SDK header value to lowercase.

anika-support: Customer on the call right now. They can't ship an SDK change quickly. Will take the pool header override if we provide exact header name/value. They want a patch from us.

lee-runtime: I'll prepare a hotfix to normalize tier values (toLowerCase) and add unit tests + e2e. Plan: canary in us-west-2 then roll. ETA ~30m for canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started canary deploy `cp-normalize-tier` on controlplane/us-west-2 by lee-runtime at 1847654385.

jordan-eng-sre: Repro steps for SRE: 
1) curl -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: Gold' -H 'X-Tenant-ID: acme-123' https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate 
-> response: 429, headers include `X-Redwood-Pool: coldpool-01` and `x-redwood-throttle: tenant-rate`.
2) curl -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: gold' -H 'X-Tenant-ID: acme-123' -> routed to `acme-prod-gold` as expected.

dino-qa: Also found related edge case: tenant metadata routing policy checks tenant.model_tier string with exact compare. I'll add case-insensitive compare there and add unit tests to avoid regressions.

anika-support: Customer confirmed temporary pool-header override worked and they rerouted traffic. They want timeline and postmortem. Ticket created: ACME-9876.

lee-runtime: Canary looks clean so far (no new 5xx or routing errors). Rolling to other regions now. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4321 (normalize-tier-values + tests) — I'll include rollback steps in PR description.

anika-support: Thanks — sending customer update now. @jordan-eng-sre please own postmortem and follow-ups (alerting + SDK guidance). :thumbsup:

jordan-eng-sre: On it. I'll assemble timeline, impact numbers (percent of requests misrouted), and add a Grafana alert to detect tier-value mismatches and a metric for fallback-to-coldpool rate. Follow-ups: add SDK note to normalize tier header values and ship small patch.
